title: Geopolitical Daily
preheader: Saudi air defenses say they intercepted it; smoke was seen near Riyadh's airport.
intro_text: Good morning. It's Sunday, September 20, 2026 — the 3 stories that matter most today, plus 8 quick updates from around the world.

stories.story_title: Houthis fire a ballistic missile at Riyadh for the first time since the war reignited
stories.why_important: Yemen's Houthis tried to hit Riyadh with a ballistic missile, and the Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted the attack. Residents heard an explosion and saw smoke near the airport. This is the first strike on the Saudi capital since fighting reopened, opening a new front in the wider Iran war.
stories.what_overlooked: Saudi Arabia confirmed the attack only hours later. Nobody has said what kind of missile it was, where it launched from, or what the intercept damaged.
stories.prediction: Watch whether the Saudi-led coalition strikes Houthi launch sites inside Yemen within the next few days.

stories.story_title: Germans vote in two states as far-right and far-left gains threaten Chancellor Merz
stories.why_important: About 3.8 million voters in Berlin and Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania are choosing state parliaments. Polls show the far-right AfD and the radical left gaining. A bad result would further weaken Chancellor Friedrich Merz, whose support was already wobbling after a defeat two weeks ago.
stories.what_overlooked: These are state votes, not national ones. But they are the clearest test yet of whether Merz's coalition can survive the year.
stories.prediction: Watch the AfD's vote share in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania and whether CDU lawmakers start questioning Merz openly.

stories.story_title: Trump blocks CNN, MS NOW and Politico reporters from the White House
stories.why_important: Journalists from three outlets were denied entry to White House grounds after Trump announced bans on them. Other US newsrooms called the move unconstitutional and an attack on a free press. It tests how far a president can legally restrict coverage of himself.
stories.what_overlooked: The White House has published no written rules for the ban. It is unclear who is next or how an outlet could appeal.
stories.prediction: Watch whether a banned outlet sues, and whether the White House press corps pushes back as a group.

quick_hits.text: North Korea fired a ballistic missile into the East Sea, Seoul said — eight days after its last launch and after rejecting a UN nuclear resolution.
Iran handed Washington seven conditions for restarting talks, including ending hostilities and unfreezing assets, and says Trump's threats will not work.
Trump said he will create an 'AI Force' and appoint an 'AI czar', calling AI safety warnings a hoax amid the race with China.
Macron visited Saint Pierre and Miquelon to reaffirm French sovereignty, meeting Canada's Mark Carney as Ottawa distances itself from Washington.
Michelle Bachelet dropped out of the race to lead the UN after weak Security Council support, ending her bid to be the first woman secretary-general.
Hundreds marched in Buenos Aires in a 'March of Anger' against President Javier Milei's austerity cuts, demanding higher wages and more public spending.
Russia's multi-day elections entered a third day, with officials reporting 49.63% turnout by midday and 3.5 million online votes already cast.
Opposition to AI is spreading, with El Pais describing a growing movement of protest and sabotage as safety warnings from researchers mount.

big_number.context: Reported turnout by midday on day three of Russia's elections — unusually high for a vote with no real opposition on the ballot.
